parts.text:
Outcome: Depressive symptoms (lower is better)

## Study A
Found: no effect
Claim: Genetically predicted 25(OH)vitamin D concentration had no causal effect on depressive symptoms.
Sentence: "MR analysis revealed no causal effects of 25(OH)vitamin D concentration, either on DS (inverse variance weighted (IVW); b = 0.025, SE = 0.038, p = 0.52) or on BD (IVW; b = 0.020, SE = 0.012, p = 0.10)."
Measured as: depressive symptoms (DS)
Population: Genetic summary data: 161,460 participants for depressive symptoms GWAS; SUNLIGHT GWAS of 79,366 subjects for 25(OH)D instruments
Intervention: Genetically predicted 25(OH)vitamin D concentration (six SNPs)
Comparator: None (Mendelian randomization)
Design: other primary study
Sample size: 322,280
baseline_vitamin_d_status: not_reported

## Study B
Found: benefit
Claim: Lower 25OHD levels were correlated with more severe depressive symptoms in first-episode psychosis patients.
Sentence: "Low 25OHD was significantly correlated with high severities of depressive (r=-0.484, p=0.004) and negative (r=-0.480, p=0.005) symptoms as well as general psychopathology (r=-0.569, p=0.001) in FEP patients."
Measured as: depression (Beck Depression Inventory)
Population: Adults aged 18-45 years with affective and non-affective first-episode psychosis presenting to an early intervention team in Portugal
Intervention: None (observational; serum 25-hydroxyvitamin D level)
Comparator: Not applicable (correlation across participants)
Design: cross-sectional study
Sample size: 66
baseline_vitamin_d_status: below_20_ng_ml
